concepts.name: Mathematical astronomy
concepts.summary: Predicting the positions of the Sun, Moon and planets, and events such as eclipses, by calculation from recorded observations.

concepts.name: The spherical Earth and its size
concepts.summary: Knowing that the Earth is a sphere and measuring its circumference.

concepts.name: Keeping the seasons by the Sun and stars
concepts.summary: Fixing the turning points of the year by watching where the Sun rises and sets on the horizon or when particular stars first appear.

concepts.name: The expanding universe
concepts.summary: Knowing that the Milky Way is one galaxy among many and that the galaxies are receding from one another.

concepts.name: The hot big bang
concepts.summary: Knowing that the universe began in a hot dense state, from the relic radiation it left behind.

concepts.name: Laws of the lever and of floating bodies
concepts.summary: Calculating balance, centres of gravity and buoyancy from mathematical laws.

concepts.name: Mathematical laws of motion
concepts.summary: Describing how bodies fall, roll and fly by mathematical laws tested against measurement.

concepts.name: Atmospheric pressure and the vacuum
concepts.summary: Knowing that the air has weight and presses on everything, and being able to make and use a vacuum.

concepts.name: Experimental optics and the theory of vision
concepts.summary: Explaining sight by light travelling in straight lines from objects into the eye, established by geometry and controlled experiment.

concepts.name: Wave theory of light
concepts.summary: Understanding light as a wave, which explains interference, diffraction and polarisation.

concepts.name: Spectrum analysis
concepts.summary: Identifying chemical elements, on Earth or in the Sun and stars, from the lines in their light.

concepts.name: Laser
concepts.summary: Producing an intense, coherent beam of light by stimulated emission.

concepts.name: Kinetic theory and statistical mechanics
concepts.summary: Explaining heat, pressure and entropy by the statistics of moving molecules.

concepts.name: Electric charge, conduction and storage
concepts.summary: Generating, conducting and storing static electric charge and explaining it as one conserved quantity.

concepts.name: Atomism
concepts.summary: Holding that all matter is built from minute indivisible particles whose combinations explain the variety of things.

concepts.name: Radioactivity
concepts.summary: Knowing that some atoms spontaneously emit radiation and change into other elements.

concepts.name: The electron
concepts.summary: Knowing that electricity is carried by a particle far lighter than any atom and present in all matter.

concepts.name: The quantum of energy
concepts.summary: Knowing that energy is exchanged between matter and light only in discrete amounts.

concepts.name: The nuclear atom
concepts.summary: Knowing that an atom is a small dense nucleus surrounded by electrons in definite energy states.

concepts.name: Laboratory alchemy and distillation
concepts.summary: Transforming, separating and purifying substances with dedicated apparatus for distilling, subliming and calcining, pursued as a systematic art with written recipes and theory.

concepts.name: Oxygen theory of combustion and the chemical element
concepts.summary: Understanding burning, rusting and breathing as combination with oxygen, with mass conserved and elements defined as substances that cannot be broken down.

concepts.name: Structural theory of organic chemistry
concepts.summary: Representing a compound by the way its atoms are bonded to each other, so that its properties and synthesis can be predicted.

concepts.name: Geological change and deep time
concepts.summary: Reading rocks, fossils and landforms as the record of slow natural change over very long spans of time.

concepts.name: Radiometric dating and the age of the Earth
concepts.summary: Measuring the age of rocks, and of the Earth itself, from the steady decay of radioactive elements.

concepts.name: Greenhouse warming by carbon dioxide
concepts.summary: Knowing that carbon dioxide and water vapour in the air trap heat, so that changing their amount changes the climate.

concepts.name: Plate tectonics
concepts.summary: Understanding the Earth's surface as rigid plates that move, creating oceans, mountains, earthquakes and volcanoes at their edges.

concepts.name: Numerical weather prediction
concepts.summary: Forecasting the weather by solving the equations of atmospheric motion on a computer.

concepts.name: Systematic natural history
concepts.summary: Describing, comparing and classifying kinds of animals and plants from direct observation, as a body of recorded knowledge.

concepts.name: Hierarchical classification with two-part names
concepts.summary: Placing every kind of organism in a nested hierarchy and giving each species a standard two-word name.

concepts.name: Microscopic life
concepts.summary: Seeing living things and structures too small for the naked eye: cells, protozoa, bacteria and sperm.

concepts.name: Cell theory
concepts.summary: Knowing that all living things are made of cells and that every cell comes from an earlier cell.

concepts.name: Microbes as the agents of fermentation and decay
concepts.summary: Knowing that fermentation and putrefaction are the work of living micro-organisms, which arise only from other micro-organisms.

concepts.name: Photosynthesis
concepts.summary: Knowing that green plants use light to build their substance from carbon dioxide and water and give off oxygen.

concepts.name: Reprogramming cells to a pluripotent state
concepts.summary: Turning a specialised adult cell back into a cell that can form any tissue.

concepts.name: Laws of heredity
concepts.summary: Knowing that traits pass between generations as discrete paired factors that separate and recombine in fixed ratios.

concepts.name: Chromosome theory of heredity
concepts.summary: Knowing that genes lie in a line on chromosomes and being able to map their positions.

concepts.name: The genetic code
concepts.summary: Knowing how the sequence of bases in DNA and RNA specifies the sequence of amino acids in a protein.

concepts.name: Programmable genome editing
concepts.summary: Cutting and rewriting a chosen DNA sequence in a living cell by supplying a short guide molecule.

concepts.name: Extinction and the succession of life
concepts.summary: Knowing that species have died out and that different assemblages of living things have followed one another through time.

concepts.name: Population genetics and the evolutionary synthesis
concepts.summary: Explaining evolution as changes in the frequencies of genes in populations under selection, mutation and chance.

concepts.name: Human origins in Africa
concepts.summary: Knowing from fossils that the human lineage arose in Africa over millions of years.

concepts.name: Biological pest control
concepts.summary: Protecting a crop by deliberately establishing the natural enemies of its pests.

concepts.name: Geography of plants and animals
concepts.summary: Explaining which living things are found where by climate, altitude and latitude.

concepts.name: The ecosystem
concepts.summary: Understanding a community of organisms and its physical setting as one system through which energy and nutrients flow along food chains.

concepts.name: The brain and nerves as the organ of sensation and movement
concepts.summary: Knowing that sensation, movement and thought depend on the brain and on nerves running to and from it.

concepts.name: The electrical nature of nerve and muscle action
concepts.summary: Knowing that nerves and muscles work by electricity generated in the living tissue.

concepts.name: The neuron doctrine
concepts.summary: Knowing that the nervous system is built of separate cells that pass signals to one another across gaps.
